To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Rh–Y zeolite catalyst is active for the ethylene hydroformilation under atmospheric pressure and the catalytic activity depends on the pretreatment conditions of the catalyst.
ethylene hydroformylations over a Rh–Y zeolite catalyst were carried out at atmospheric pressure.

ethylene hydroformylations in Rh–Y zeolite are catalyzed by a stable species, which is formed in situ and is not affected by the pretreatments of the catalyst, but the activity of the catalyst is remarkably affected by pretreatments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the catalytic hydroformylation of ethylene over the Rh–Y zeolite.
the effects of pretreatment of the Rh–Y zeolite on its catalytic activity for ethylene hydro-formylation under atmospheric pressure.
the effects of the pretreatment of Rh-Y zeolite on the activity for ethylene hydro-formylation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the catalytic activity of the Rh–Y zeolite is determined by the concentration of active Rh–H species, the amount of which depends on the concentration of the Rh–H species and the concentration of the active Rh–H sites.
the catalytic activity for ethylene hydro-formylation is enhanced by the He–H _{2} pretreatment at 453–523 K and the activity is reduced by the He–CO pretreatment.
the catalytic activity for the hydroformylation is controlled by the surface species of Rh–Y, and the surface species are strongly affected by the pretreatments of the catalyst.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Rh–Y zeolite catalysts are highly selective for the linear product and the catalytic activity is affected by the pretreatments of the zeolite.
the Rh–Y zeolite catalyzed hydroformylation is the best example of the hydroformylation under atmospheric pressure.
the active species is generated by the interaction of the Rh cation and H2 on the zeolite surface, and the active sites are blocked with CO or C2H4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Rh–Y system is an excellent catalyst for ethylene hydro-formylation under mild reaction conditions.

the pretreatments with H2 or CO at 453 K and 1 atm, which are usually used for activating the Rh–Y zeolite catalyst, are not effective for enhancing the catalytic activity for ethylene hydrofomylation.
the pretreatment of Rh-Y catalysts with hydrogen is a promising method for enhancing its activity for ethylene hydro formylation.
